info.name: aBILLity API test
info.description:
Tests the aBILLity half of the company name sync on its own - credentials, company id, and the rename the Worker performs - with no Autotask or Cloudflare involved.

Checked against api.abillity.co.uk/GettingStarted: GET returns a CompanyView with Name at
the top level, PATCH updates selected details, PUT would replace ALL details, and the id is
an integer. Name is limited to 50 characters.

SETUP
  Variables tab: systemInformation, abillityUserName, abillityPassword, companyId, and testName.

ORDER
  0 checks the credentials against /site, the endpoint aBILLity's own examples use.
    Run it first when anything is failing - it isolates auth from the company endpoint.
  1 reads the company - name, LastUpdated, flags and dates - and stores the name.
    Read-only. Run this alone whenever you just want to check what aBILLity holds.
  2 renames it. THIS WRITES TO LIVE BILLING DATA.
  3 puts the original name back.

Run 1 before 2, and 3 straight after, on a company you are willing to rename. If you only want to check the credentials, run 1 and stop.

request.description:
The endpoint every example in aBILLity's own docs uses. Run it FIRST when something is wrong - it separates 'my credentials/headers are wrong' from 'something is wrong with the company endpoint'.

Read-only.

Note there is no Content-Type header here. This is a GET with no body, and sending Content-Type on a bodyless request upsets some ASP.NET stacks.

200 - auth works. The problem is elsewhere.
401 - credentials or permissions.
500 - aBILLity threw an unhandled error. Most often SystemInformation is wrong or missing, since that is what selects which system to connect to - a bad value can fail inside the API rather than come back as a clean 401.

exec: console.log('Auth works. Your SystemInformation, username and password are all accepted.');
console.log('If a company request still fails, the problem is that request, not your credentials.');
console.log('401 - bad credentials OR no permissions. aBILLity uses 401 for both.');
console.log('500 - aBILLity threw an error rather than rejecting you. Check, in order:');
console.log('  1. SystemInformation - is it exactly the value your admin gave you?');
console.log('     It selects the system to connect to; a wrong one can fail inside the API.');
console.log('  2. Header names: SystemInformation, username, password - no typos, no extra spaces.');
console.log('  3. Postman Authorization tab set to "No Auth" - anything else adds a');
console.log('  4. No Content-Type header on a GET (this request deliberately omits it).');
console.log('Response is HTML, not JSON - you are seeing a server error page.');
console.log('Read the body; ASP.NET often names the underlying fault in it.');

request.description:
GET api/company/{id} - the details of one company. Read-only, changes nothing, so run it as often as you like.

Use it on its own to check what aBILLity currently holds for a company, or before requests 2 and 3 so the original name is captured.

LastUpdated is the useful one when testing the sync: after renaming the company in Autotask, this should show a timestamp of a moment ago. If the name changed but LastUpdated is old, you are looking at the wrong company.

401 = bad credentials OR no company permissions (aBILLity uses 401 for both).
404 = no such company, or no companies in this database.

exec: if (code === 401) { console.log('401 - bad credentials OR no company permissions. aBILLity uses 401 for both.'); }
if (code === 403) { console.log('403 - credentials valid, but not allowed to read this company.'); }
if (code === 404) { console.log('404 - no company ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('companyId') + ', or no companies in this database.'); }
if (code === 405) { console.log('405 - no GET on this endpoint. Skip to request 2, but note that'); }
if (code === 405) { console.log('      nothing will capture the original name, so restoring is manual.'); }
// CompanyView returns everything at the top level.
console.log('Testing a sync? LastUpdated should be a moment ago if the rename just landed.');
console.log('Name stored in {{originalName}} - request 3 restores it.');
console.log('Read OK but no Name field found. Check the raw body below.');
pm.test('Has a name', function () { pm.expect(name, 'no Name in the response').to.be.ok; });

request.description:
The exact call the Worker makes when an Autotask company is renamed.

*** THIS CHANGES LIVE BILLING DATA. ***

Run request 1 first so the original name is captured, then request 3 to put it back.

aBILLity caps the name at 50 characters and the Worker truncates to match - keep {{testName}} under 50 unless you are deliberately testing that.

exec: console.log('Rename accepted - this is what the Worker does.');
console.log('The Worker would log this and return "sync failed".');

request.description:
Puts the name back to whatever request 1 captured in {{originalName}}.

If {{originalName}} is empty, request 1 did not capture it - set the name by hand in aBILLity instead of running this.

exec: console.log('WARNING: {{originalName}} is empty - this request just sent a blank name.');
console.log('Fix the company name by hand in aBILLity.');
console.log('RESTORE FAILED (' + pm.response.code + '). The company is still renamed.');
console.log('Put it back by hand in aBILLity.');
